gapTargets.finding: The Production Ready card specifically associates mature reliability with commercial/industrial deployment; current Q003/Q004/Q076 cover other cards and capability caveats, not that association.
gapTargets.repairTarget: Extend a suitable feature-card item with a source-scoped production-readiness distinction. Do not assert automatic reliability or deadlines.

gapTargets.finding: The separate five-node drawing links Camera–Lidar, Lidar–Control, Camera–SLAM and Lidar–Nav. Q011 treats node/package roles; p186 questions concern a different four-node directed graph.
gapTargets.repairTarget: Assess an actual adjacency or absent edge in this drawing. No arrowheads or topic names are supplied, so do not invent publication directions.

gapTargets.finding: The text and figure explicitly assign Vision Node to GPU and Path Planning Node to CPU and mention different nodes/cores. Existing questions discuss Jetson versus microcontroller but not this within-host allocation.
gapTargets.repairTarget: Extend a hardware-allocation question with the shown GPU/CPU roles. Do not promise automatic pinning, optimal scheduling or timing guarantees.

gapTargets.finding: The screenshot ends with if __name__ == __main__: main(). Q016 tests lifecycle order and Q017 names but does not test direct execution versus importing the module.
gapTargets.repairTarget: A small source-code control-flow application can assess whether main runs under the stated __name__ value. Avoid a second lifecycle-order duplicate.

gapTargets.finding: The final bullet motivates optimized message structures by the cost of moving 4K/high-bandwidth data between AI nodes and hardware drivers. Current Q020/Q021 only test interface agreement and message-type roles.
gapTargets.repairTarget: Assess data-movement overhead as the stated motivation, not financial cost, automatic zero-copy, exact bandwidth or a guarantee of unlimited throughput.

gapTargets.finding: The phone-call discussion permits multiple clients for the depicted intended named service server. Current Q031 identifies one request/response pair but does not test that client fan-in pattern.
gapTargets.repairTarget: Assess only the course-described intended server/multiple-client arrangement, not an enforced global uniqueness theorem. Keep source issue08 caveat.

gapTargets.finding: The screenshot explicitly creates a server and client with AddTwoInts and add, binds handle_service to the server, and returns the response object. Existing questions cover arithmetic, availability, future and parameter but not endpoint construction/matching.
gapTargets.repairTarget: Extend a code question to distinguish create_service/create_client roles and their matching type/name, or returned response versus request. Do not invent automatic future completion.

gapTargets.finding: The sensing bullet names USB or CSI as example ports linking sensors with Jetson before data are published. Current Q042/Q069 test functional stage order but no physical interface distinction.
gapTargets.repairTarget: Add or extend one source-scoped sensor-interface item. Do not claim every listed sensor supports both interfaces, or confuse physical port with ROS topic.

additionalSourceCautions.note: Connectivity strokes have no arrowheads or topic labels; only adjacency can be asserted.

The Jetson-to-controller figure label Serial Data / PWM is broader than the prose assigning precise PWM timing to Arduino. Existing Q043/Q044 use the prose responsibility split rather than asserting that Jetson generates every PWM edge.
The screenshot includes the final argument10 but does not explain its API semantics. No source-only gap requires unstated QoS implementation knowledge.

nonblockingEditorialNotes.note: The justification sentence about a service response not being a package is true but tangential to the current package-versus-running-node distractor. Remove it during any otherwise-needed revision; this alone is not a correctness flag.

duplicateInflationChecks.finding: Signed operand variant of the same addition handler, retained as practice but not a new concept.
Reciprocal rates and endpoint counts belong to the same rate/event-count family, not four unique concepts; endpoint and two-stream comparison remain distinct examination angles.
Summary loop restates sensing/computation/actuation; no new concept is counted solely from p209.
